# test-summary

Run a test command; return pass/fail counts, the first failure and its trace head, log path.

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Help |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--cmd` | str | yes |  | Test command, run through the shell from the current directory |
| `--timeout` | int | no | `300` | Seconds before the command is killed |

Run it from the repo root:

```
caveman-blocks run test-summary --cmd <str>
```

It prints one JSON object with the keys passed, failed, skipped, first_failure, exit, log, duration_s.

Without the CLI, `python3 .blocks/test-summary.py --cmd <str>` runs the same file, but nothing is enforced: no effects gate, no path confinement, no output cap.
